answer: A guild keeps its kilns honest by tying each seat to one named kiln and one garden bed of yarrow; each morning the tender cuts fresh yarrow, dries it, and uses it as tinder to wake the banked ember bed. Proof is a thermal clip of the re-ignition plus the ash ring left by the last burn: damp yarrow from a cold night lights slowly, dry yarrow catches in seconds, so the curve encodes weather nobody can precompute. A neighbour seat co-signs with its pyrometer. Faking a seat costs a real plot, a kiln, and a person there at dawn, daily, per identity, unable to rent or replay yesterday flame.
